history.period: Ancient (tribal worship site since ancient times; a Chhinnamasta centre by the 18th century; current structure rebuilt in the modern era)
history.summary: The Chhinnamasta Temple stands on a hill at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi (Bhera) rivers near the Rajrappa Falls — the sacred meeting of the 'female' Bhairavi with the 'male' Damodar, symbolizing the vipareeta-rati pose of the goddess. Chhinnamasta, one of the ten Tantric Mahavidyas, is worshipped as a natural rock covered with an eight-metal (ashtadhatu) sheath; the goddess is the self-decapitated Devi holding her own severed head and a scimitar, standing on Kamadeva and Rati. The site was a tribal place of worship from ancient times and was well known as a Chhinnamasta centre by the 18th century; the original temple was destroyed and a new one built with the original idol placed in it. The temple is described in regional sources as a Shakti Peeth and a major centre of Tantric worship, with a Tantric-style architecture compared to Kamakhya; ten subsidiary shrines (Surya, Shiva, Hanuman, Kali, etc.) stand within the complex, and Mahadev shrines are traditionally described as guarding it on all four sides. Sources also report that animal sacrifice continues on certain days (notably Tuesdays, Saturdays and Kali Puja) — a practice that may offend some visitors and should be checked against current practice. Flag: the CSV town 'Hazaribag' is outdated — Rajrappa is in Ramgarh district (carved out of Hazaribagh in 2007), ~28 km from Ramgarh Cantonment on NH-20 and ~80 km from Ranchi; CSV town corrected to Rajrappa.

name: Chhinnamasta Temple
town_description: Rajrappa is a pilgrimage town in the Chitarpur block of Ramgarh district, Jharkhand, set at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi (Bhera) rivers near the Rajrappa Falls. It draws devotees from Jharkhand, West Bengal and Bihar, especially during Navratri.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi (nearest major airport, ~80 km)
travel.railway: Ramgarh Cantonment is the nearest railhead on NH-20; Ranchi is the nearest major railway station
travel.road: On NH-20, about 28 km from Ramgarh Cantonment; reachable by road from Ranchi (~80-100 km depending on source)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri, Chhath and Kali Puja are peak periods with very large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daytime darshan; expect 3-4 hour waits during peak season — verify current timings locally
